The UI/UX Design internship in short

In the SkillMe UI/UX Design internship you build one of 3 projects, such as CanteenQ: Campus Canteen Pre-order App, a project where you design a mobile app that lets students order canteen food ahead and skip the queue. In week 1 you talk to real students about canteen queues, turn what you hear into a persona and a clear problem statement, and map the ordering flow. By week 4 you link your screens into a clickable prototype, test it with 3 people, fix the biggest issues and write a case study. Each milestone is posted on LinkedIn and checked against that week's checklist before it counts. Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month.

Week by week

What each week of the UI/UX Design internship covers

Shown for CanteenQ: Campus Canteen Pre-order App. The other projects follow the same four-week shape.

  1. Week 1 of 4

    User Research and Problem Statement

    Beginner2-3 hours

    Talk to real students about canteen queues, turn what you hear into a persona and a clear problem statement, and map the ordering flow. Good design starts with understanding people, not with screens.

    What you learn

    • Planning and running short user interviews
    • Creating a persona from real findings
    • Writing a problem statement
    • Mapping a simple user flow

    What you submit

    • Interview questions and notes or survey results
    • Affinity map in FigJam
    • Persona and problem statement
    • User flow diagram
    How week 1 is reviewed
    • At least 3 interviews or 15 survey responses are recorded
    • Findings are grouped into at least 3 themes
    • The persona includes goals, frustrations and a real quote
    • The user flow covers the full order journey plus one alternate path

    Stretch goal: Visit the canteen at peak time, time the queue and add these observations to your research.

  2. Week 2 of 4

    Low-fidelity Wireframes

    Beginner+2-3 hours

    Turn your user flow into grayscale wireframes for the main screens. Wireframes let you test layout and flow quickly before spending time on colours and details.

    What you learn

    • Information hierarchy and layout
    • Using frames and basic shapes in Figma
    • Sketching multiple ideas before choosing one
    • Linking wireframes to the user flow

    What you submit

    • Photo of paper sketches
    • Figma file with at least 6 wireframe screens
    • Short notes on feedback from one person
    How week 2 is reviewed
    • At least 6 screens cover the full flow from Week 1
    • Each screen has one clear primary action
    • Screens are in grayscale with no final visual styling
    • At least one change was made based on feedback

    Stretch goal: Add wireframes for an empty cart and an item-sold-out state.

  3. Week 3 of 4

    High-fidelity UI and Mini Design System

    Intermediate2-3 hours

    Create a small design system with colours, a type scale and reusable components, then use it to turn your wireframes into polished screens. You will also check basic accessibility.

    What you learn

    • Colour styles and text styles
    • Reusable components and variants
    • Auto layout for flexible buttons and cards
    • Basic accessibility: colour contrast and tap target size

    What you submit

    • Design System page with colours, type and components
    • At least 6 high-fidelity screens
    • Screenshot of contrast checks
    How week 3 is reviewed
    • All colours and text on screens use saved styles
    • At least 4 reusable components exist, one with variants
    • Buttons and cards use auto layout
    • Body text meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio
    • Tap targets are at least 44x44 pt

    Stretch goal: Create a dark mode version of two screens using the same components.

  4. Week 4 of 4

    Prototype, Usability Test and Case Study

    Intermediate+2-3 hours

    Link your screens into a clickable prototype, test it with 3 people, fix the biggest issues and write a case study. This shows your full process from research to tested design.

    What you learn

    • Prototyping with interactions in Figma
    • Running a simple usability test
    • Prioritising and fixing issues
    • Writing a UX case study

    What you submit

    • Clickable Figma prototype link
    • Usability test notes for 3 testers
    • Before/after screenshots of fixes
    • Published case study link
    How week 4 is reviewed
    • A tester can complete an order in the prototype without help
    • 3 usability tests are documented with issues found
    • At least 3 issues are fixed and shown before and after
    • The case study covers every stage from research to testing

    Stretch goal: Measure task completion time for each tester before and after your fixes.

Is it for you?

UI/UX Design internship: questions and answers

What will I build in the UI/UX Design internship?

You are assigned one of 3 projects: CanteenQ: Campus Canteen Pre-order App, HabitNest: Simple Habit Tracker App or LocalFix: Local Service Website Redesign. Each is a single project built up over four weekly milestones, so each week adds to the last.

What skills will I learn in the UI/UX Design internship?

The UI/UX Design internship works with Figma, Research and Prototyping. Week 1: planning and running short user interviews; creating a persona from real findings. Week 2: information hierarchy and layout; using frames and basic shapes in Figma. Week 3: colour styles and text styles; reusable components and variants. Week 4: prototyping with interactions in Figma; running a simple usability test.

Do I need experience to apply for the UI/UX Design internship?

You need the basics of Figma, Research and Prototyping, not prior internship experience. Week 1 starts at beginner level, where you talk to real students about canteen queues, turn what you hear into a persona and a clear problem statement, and map the ordering flow. Week 4 reaches intermediate+ level. A short screening quiz (8 questions, about 5 minutes) checks you are ready to start.

How is each UI/UX Design milestone reviewed?

Every week has a checklist, and a milestone is approved only when it meets all of it. For week 1 of CanteenQ: Campus Canteen Pre-order App, that means: at least 3 interviews or 15 survey responses are recorded; findings are grouped into at least 3 themes; the persona includes goals, frustrations and a real quote; the user flow covers the full order journey plus one alternate path. Reviewers include engineers who work at Walmart, Google and LinkedIn, and work that misses the bar comes back with notes.

What can I put on my resume after the UI/UX Design internship?

Each approved milestone gives you a line you can back up with a public LinkedIn post: Interviewed students to understand canteen queue problems; Created a research-based persona and problem statement; Mapped the full pre-order user flow in FigJam; Sketched and compared multiple layout ideas on paper; Built 6 low-fidelity wireframes in Figma for a canteen pre-order app; Improved the flow based on early feedback; Built a mini design system with colour styles, a type scale and components; Designed 6 high-fidelity screens using auto layout; Checked colour contrast and tap target sizes for accessibility; Built a clickable Figma prototype for a canteen pre-order app; Ran usability tests with 3 students and fixed the top issues; Published a full UX case study from research to tested design.

What are the other projects in the UI/UX Design internship?

HabitNest: Simple Habit Tracker App: Design a friendly mobile app that helps students build and keep daily habits. LocalFix: Local Service Website Redesign: Redesign the website of a local business such as a clinic, coaching centre or cafe so customers find what they need faster. Every project follows the same four-week shape, with one reviewed milestone a week.

Is the UI/UX Design internship paid? Is there a stipend?

Top performers earn a stipend of up to $100 a month. It is performance-based: 8–10 interns are picked each month from those who complete the internship and hold an issued certificate. It is not paid to every intern.

How much time does it take?

4 weeks, one milestone a week, each planned for about 2-3 hours. It is fully remote and open worldwide, so you work around college or a job.
